action: No action needed; for awareness. Washington organisations: review breach-notice obligations (reporting is required when more than 500 residents are affected).
date_note: Date of the Insurance Journal article on the report; the report's own date was not read
exec: Cyberattacks and ransomware drove most reported breaches in Washington state over the past year.
plain: Washington's attorney general reports 197 data breaches over one year, with more than 3.5 million notices sent to residents. Cyberattacks, mostly ransomware, were the top cause.

key_findings: 197 data breaches reported to the Washington AG's Office between July 24, 2025 and July 23, 2026, with more than 3.5 million notices sent to residents.
Cyberattacks accounted for 139 incidents; ransomware was the most common method, responsible for 86 incidents.
Social Security numbers were exposed in 148 breaches; no breach affecting 1 million or more Washington residents was reported.
Both breach and notice counts declined from the previous reporting year, per the report as relayed.
report.publisher: Insurance Journal (on Washington Attorney General's Office annual Data Breach Report)
recommendations: The report recommends updates to the state's data breach notification laws.

summary: The Washington Attorney General's Office annual Data Breach Report, as covered by Insurance Journal, counts 197 breaches reported to the state between July 24, 2025 and July 23, 2026, with more than 3.5 million notices to residents. Cyberattacks caused 139 incidents, 86 of them ransomware. Both counts fell from the prior year.
title: Washington AG report: 197 data breaches and more than 3.5 million notices in the year to July 2026

validation.note: Insurance Journal only; the Attorney General's report itself was not opened.
